steps.content:
N.F. ██, █/██
███ Highlands
Trench Bunker

steps.speaker: Agitated Soldier
steps.content: ******* hell. I signed up for the pay, not a coffin. I'm not dying in this ****hole...
The door slams open. On the shelf, labeled bottles tremble and clatter; a few pitch forward and shatter on the floorboards, their last few drops bleeding into the wood.
Forty-nine days into this posting.
She dives for the cabinet against the wall, wrenching the door open. Her hands scramble through the hollow contents: a skeletal sewing kit, gutted cans, a flattened cigarette pack...
Then, her fingers close on a bottle of anesthetic. It, too, is empty.

steps.speaker: Agitated Soldier
steps.content: ...Are you ******* kidding me? Nothing! There's nothing left!
The door opens again. A gaunt man rushes forward and grabs her arm.

steps.speaker: Gaunt Soldier
steps.content: Freyna! Freyna, take a breath!

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Get off me!

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Ranor, you and that woman wanna lick Fraser's boots? Fine. But I'll be damned if I rot here with you!

steps.speaker: Ranor
steps.content: And go where? You saw the scouts. It's a death sentence out there!

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: I'd rather take my chances than starve waiting on a miracle!

Ranor draws breath to argue, and freezes at the sound of footsteps in the doorway. He knows without turning. He stands, hands pressed flat to his sides, posture rigid. Beside him, Freyna only rummages faster.
A woman pauses on the threshold, her gaze a winter chill over the shattered mess. Then she moves, crossing the room in swift strides to clamp a hand around Freyna's wrist.
The grip is vice-tight, draining the color from Freyna's skin. Slowly, Freyna raises her eyes, giving a look of simmering contempt.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: —But I guess our dear Captain doesn't get that.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: We follow orders. That is the job.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: Save that ******* lecture for the graves!

Freyna wrenches her wrist free. From the cabinet, she snatches the ragged remains of a combat jacket and hurls it between them. The fabric is stiff, the bloodstains dried to a cracked black. The name once stitched across the chest is now illegible.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: He... died with honor.

steps.speaker: Freyna
steps.content: ******* bullshit! Anyone with eyes can see it! We've been left to die! If reinforcements were coming, they'd be here a month ago! If you'd just given the order to fall back—

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: Enough! There are no cowards under my command. Look at your insignia. Remember why we stand here! We fight... for Fraser's future.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: This is the battle that matters. Let me be clear: in my unit, there are soldiers. Not deserters. Anyone who tries to leave...

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: ...will be dealt with as the law allows.
Freyna holds the woman's gaze, unblinking. Her jaw is a locked vise, her silence louder than any shout. Ranor cannot bear it; he turns his face away.

steps.speaker: Captain
steps.content: The Senate's strategy is beyond our sight. Their promise will be honored. No matter what, we will hold—

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color>. That's where we're headed.

"Ten o'clock, roughly five kilometers out." She makes it sound so simple. But you lack her preternatural vision. Squinting through the binoculars, you sweep the horizon—once, twice, again—finding only an endless, rippling expanse of gray-yellow rock.
Finally, you lower the lenses, defeated.

Behind you on the farland watchtower platform, Helga is already on to more tangible work. She's tilted back in her seat, foot braced against her toolbox, carefully tinkering a music box brought to her by one of the settlement's children.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Place like that has always been a magnet for a fight. In my day, the old Fraser hands used to say that heading to Alsa meant you'd already dug half your own grave.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: A damn mass grave like that, plus all the Mania weapons they used... Yeah, Alsa's been Corruptor territory for years now.
A soft click echoes in the quiet. Helga gives the toy a gentle, content shake, then glances up. Your gazes finally meet.
She catches your bewildered expression and lets out a low chuckle. Pushing herself to her feet, she rests a hand on your shoulder and points a decisive finger toward the far horizon.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Follow my finger... Ease left a little... more... There. See it now, kid?

Following the farlands' declaration of independence, Fraser extended surface-level recognition while simultaneously imposing an undeclared blockade through various covert measures.

This ensured that, despite Farland Researcher Hypatia's capacity to locate Hypercube deposits, critical supplies remained inaccessible, threatening the farlands with catastrophic famine.

Hope emerged when farland scouts identified an unpatrolled route circumventing Fraser's primary checkpoints, almost as if Fraser had deliberately left it open.

Its neglect was no accident. The path traversed the <color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color>, a region notoriously saturated with Corruptors.

Clearing a Corruptor zone of this scale was beyond the farlands' capabilities, but for a seasoned Bureau Chief like you, it was routine. Armed with proper equipment and experience, the task required minimal support.

That is why, one week ago, Helga showed up at your door alone.

Having spent years building a formidable farland underground network in Fraser, she now stood as the first Speaker of the Farland Assembly, here to formally request your aid.

You agreed to assist in a personal capacity, as official diplomatic channels between DisCity and the farlands did not yet exist. With Helga personally vouching for your safety, you've brought enough purification devices to cleanse the highlands. All that remains is to trigger them at the right moment.

steps.speaker: Deep Female Voice
steps.content: Speaker, we've arrived.
You and Helga turn to see three silhouettes framed in the watchtower doorway.
Helga swiftly seals the music box inside her toolbox before stepping forward, deliberately placing herself in front of you. With an open-armed gesture, she begins the introductions.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: This is Tavera. Finest spear in all the settlements. She'll be watching our backs on this run.
The tall woman at the center plants her spear on the ground. Then, inclining her head and shoulders, she offers you a slight bow.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: This one's Milonn. His people live around these parts. No one knows the path to Alsa like he does.
A short, scrawny man gives you a nervous nod, his whole frame seeming to shiver with the motion.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: And this is Vester. Sent by the Assembly. Specifically to...

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ...keep an eye on me for this mission.
The remaining man, lean and wiry, fixes his gaze on you, his face twisting into a forced smile.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Then you must be—

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: This is ${PlayerName}. Our Mania expert.
The success of this mission will determine the very survival of the farlands. That is why each major settlement has sent a representative to support the operation.
But old wounds bleed fresh. The war may be over on paper, yet the chasm between the farlands and DisCity runs as deep as ever.
Consider Tavera: Helga describes her as courageous and unshakably loyal—a loyalty that manifests as a pure, venomous hatred for anything Disian.
You cannot reveal you are from DisCity. So while your role on the team remains that of a Mania expert, you are not the Chief of MBCC. Instead, you are—

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Also my grandson.
Helga beams at you with a grandmotherly warmth so genuine, you could almost believe you were family.
...Granny.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: This is the first I've heard of you having a grandson, Speaker.
steps.female_content: This is the first I've heard of you having a granddaughter, Speaker.

steps.content: Helga releases a booming laugh and sweeps you into a tight, engulfing hug.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Every kid in our camp is one of mine.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Your camp had a Mania expert all this time? Funny how you've never mentioned such a valuable asset before.
Vester presses you, but you hold your ground. You came ready for this, and your rehearsed reply comes with practiced ease.
I got captured by a DisCity unit once, one that handled Mania. A blessing in disguise, I guess. Picked up a thing or two just by listening.
At your words, Milonn flinches. He has been trembling since he entered, and now the last of the color drains from his face, leaving him deathly pale.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: And you call yourself an expert?! <size=30>Y-you're joking, right...?</size>

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: "A thing or two" isn't good enough. Speaker, can this ki— can this expert really handle it?
Every eye locks onto you at once.

The mission itself is simple by your assessment. But you're playing the part of a naive farlander with only surface-level knowledge, so you pause, consider your options, and then adopt your most guileless expression.
Guess we'll find out soon enough, won't we?
Milonn's face goes even paler.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Relax. I trust him.

Helga's arm wraps around your shoulders, giving a firm squeeze. Along with the solid weight comes a peculiar scent from her jacket—the sharp tang of machine oil mingled with the earthy warmth of leftover stew.

steps.speaker: Hyenas
steps.content: Woo—! Woo-ooop! Wooop!
You and Helga peer down from the tower. Below, the hyena pack guarding the post has clustered, their eerie cries rising in a chorus.
Flanked by the animals, a massive, hunched figure is shuffling toward the outpost gate.
Helga snatches her toolbox and is already rushing down the stairs, the weight on your shoulders vanishing with her. You bolt after her, and after a moment of hesitation, the other three follow.
[Downstairs]

A deafening bang echoes as the door downstairs bursts open. You can finally see the figure clearly: a dazed young man staggering under the weight of a body, slick with blood, slumped across his shoulders. The blood falls in a grim, steady rhythm onto the floorboards.

steps.speaker: Panicked Young Man
steps.content: Granny... Granny! It's Vigne... He's not gonna make it...!

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: When the hell did you two sneak out?!

steps.speaker: Panicked Young Man
steps.content: We didn't go far! ...We saw the food running low, and the next shipment's days off, so we thought we'd try to hunt something, and then... and then...
He can't utter another word. His body sags, then collapses. Kneeling there, he covers his mouth, a muffled, wrenching noise escaping him—the sound of grief and sickness warring in his throat.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, Tavera, push the tables together. Milonn, grab that canvas off the wall.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ...Milonn? Milonn?!
On the floor, Milonn is a portrait of panic, mumbling and scuttling backward like a crab.
Seeing this, Vester clicks his tongue in irritation. He strides to the wall, yanks down the nailed canvas, and lets it snap open. Together, you and Tavera heave the wounded man onto the rough cloth.
The injuries are brutal: gouges so deep they glint with bone, the signature work of Corruptors. Miraculously, the skin shows no sickly bloom of Mania.
You remember your duty, fetching the Bureau-issued medicine from your kit and carefully administering the dose to his lips. It's a stopgap, not a cure, but it will prevent further Mania infection.
All the while, you sense the weight of Vester's sidelong gaze.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: That medicine... looks like quality stuff.
He wants to say more, but the harsh rip of tearing gauze silences him. Helga shoulders Vester aside without a glance, clamping the bandages against the ravaged flesh with immediate pressure.
Blood blooms through the cloth, dyeing her hands red, yet her motions remain steady and precise. Gradually, the wounded man's agonized sounds fade into ragged breaths.
Finished, she finally looks down. Her eyes settle on the other youth, who remains curled on the floor, still weeping.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: There, there... It's not your fault.

Her hand instinctively lifts to offer a pat of comfort, but she halts, seeing the dark blood caked in the lines of her palm. A beat passes. She simply wipes her hands clean on her trousers and releases a quiet, weary sigh.
The thud of a spear butt against the floor breaks the silence. Tavera stands rigid, staring at the bloodstains on the ground, her jaw clenched with fury.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Damn them...! Those cursed monsters... and those Fraser bastards!

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Looks like Corruptors are already prowling near the outpost. We can't waste any more time. We need to clear out Alsa now.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: N-no... I only agreed to guide! This is suicide! I'm not going... <size=45>I won't do it!</size>

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: You spineless worm! You disgrace every farlander alive...!

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ...If he doesn't want to go, let him stay.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: R-really...? Then I'm staying!

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Vester, what about you? ...What's with the shifty eyes? Spit it out.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: I haven't decided yet.
He shrugs, feigning innocence.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Going or staying, both look like bad moves right now. I'd rather not gamble my neck.
Helga's lips twist into a scornful smirk, and she lets out a cold scoff.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You just don't want to be the one left holding the bag, do you?
Finally, Helga turns to you.

Your gaze sweeps over the farlanders before you—faces etched with anger, anxiety, and at least one with a hostility you don't understand. You then look at Milonn, huddled and shivering against the wall.
It's clear: you can't place your faith in them.
I don't think we're ready yet. Maybe we should wait a little longer.
Vester lets out a whistle at your words.
Helga holds your gaze, silent, waiting for more until the silence stretches taut.
Only then does she lower her eyes to the dried blood on the floor. She shakes her head, slowly, deliberately.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ...We can't wait. This is our last chance. Several camps have only a few weeks' worth of rations left.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: If we keep dragging our feet, the Corruptors won't need to lift a finger. We'll starve ourselves to death.
After a heavy moment of quiet, she comes to you, reaches up, and gives your shoulder a firm squeeze.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ...But still, thank you.
With that, she picks up the toolbox at her feet. Her fingers linger on the handle, hesitating.
A beam of sunlight falls across her shoulder. Finally, she straightens, her voice crisp once more.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Tavera, let's go.
Tavera follows close behind. As she passes, you feel the weight of her scrutiny lingering on you.
—Or perhaps it's just your imagination. You're an outsider here. What reason do you have to feel guilty? And who is she to judge you?

You force yourself to ignore Vester's meaningful stare burning into your back, and the stifled groans of the wounded man. Ahead, the two figures grow smaller and smaller until they're no longer of your concern.
Just like the fate of the farlands.
You study the faces before you: a mosaic of fear, doubt, anger, and defiance, all knotted together. It is like staring at a reflection of the farlands themselves.
There's no turning back now. Time to move.
Vester glances at you, then at Helga. A grin pulls at the corner of his mouth.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Well, if our expert says so, I suppose I'd better tag along and see this through myself.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Now you're talking. Hmph... Four's a good number. More room in the back, at least.
With your gear secured, you take a step toward the door. Before your foot can land, a pair of arms dart out from the shadows and seize your leg in a desperate, clinging hold.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: Wait! Wait... Don't leave me here. What if...
He lowers his voice and glances back at the young man lying on the table.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: <size=30>What if that kid turns into one of them? What then?</size>
His sincerity is undeniable; the man clearly values his own skin above all else. You suppress a sigh. It's best Helga didn't hear that.
Bending down, you work his desperate hands loose from your calf.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: No...! Please! Take me with—
Then, grasping his thin, bony fingers, you haul him to his feet.
Let's go.
